§3.4 The Sidecar

📚 Document rule — needs other pages of the document; decided once and applied on every page

output-the-sidecar · output output-model boxes sidecar

✅ Normative

When boxes are requested, the output MUST include a sidecar: a structured file that lists, page by page, every element with its class, its Markdown and its box. The sidecar is the source the Markdown is rendered from; the Markdown MUST be exactly the concatenation of the sidecar's element Markdown in reading order, each element preceded by its inline box anchor, with pages joined as Markdown Rendering§3.2 requires.

The sidecar is secondary to the rest of this protocol: the rules that matter are how the document is interpreted and rendered, and what a box covers. This note fixes only what a sidecar must carry. Its encoding is the page-and-items structure LlamaParse already returns, normalised.

Contents

Level Carries
Document its pages, in order
Page 1-based page number; page width and height; printed page number when requested — see Printed Page Numbers§6.6; line_numbers when requested — see Pleading Line Numbers§5.8
Element class — see Elements§3.1; its Markdown; its box; finer boxes at the requested granularity
Box x, y, w, h in the page's coordinate space, origin top-left
Table element additionally continuesFromPreviousPage and continuesOnNextPage, booleans — see Cross-Page Tables§4.3
Finer box as a box, plus the character range of the element's Markdown it covers (startIndex, endIndex, end exclusive, counted in the element's Markdown including its syntax) 
{"page": 3, "width": 612, "height": 792, "printedPageNumber": "iv",
 "items": [{"type": "Section-header", "md": "## 9.2 Pressure",
            "bBox": {"x": 72, "y": 80, "w": 200, "h": 18},
            "layoutAwareBbox": [{"x": 72, "y": 80, "w": 200, "h": 18, "startIndex": 3, "endIndex": 15}]}]}
  • Every element of the Markdown MUST correspond to one sidecar item, and every item to one element.
  • Character ranges MUST point into the element's own Markdown, so any span of the Markdown resolves to a box.

Boxes in the Markdown itself

When boxes are requested, the Markdown MUST also carry each element's box inline, so that a single Markdown file is traceable on its own: each element is preceded by an HTML comment anchor holding the same box as the sidecar.

<!-- el p=3 x=72 y=80 w=200 h=18 -->
## 9.2 Pressure

The anchors are invisible when rendered and are stripped when the Markdown is given to a model that does not need them. When boxes are not requested, the Markdown carries no anchors.
